proposals.before: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiayou, Emperor Renzong went in person to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the xiá merging sacrifice. Chief Councilor Fu Bi served as Grandee of the Xiá Rite; Han Qi as Master of Ceremonies; Privy Council Commissioner Song Qi as Master of Insignia; Vice Grand Councilor Zeng Gongliang as Master of Bridge Roads and Relay Arrangements; and Vice Privy Council Commissioner Cheng Kan as Master of the Imperial Guard.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiayou, Emperor Renzong went in person to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the xiá merging sacrifice. Chief Councilor Fu Bi served as Grandee of the Xiá Rite; Han Qi as Master of Ceremonies; Privy Council Commissioner Song Xiang as Master of Insignia; Vice Grand Councilor Zeng Gongliang as Master of Bridge Roads and Relay Arrangements; and Vice Privy Council Commissioner Cheng Kan as Master of the Imperial Guard.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宋庠 is Song Xiang; Song Qi (宋祁) is a different person.

proposals.before: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiayou, Emperor Renzong personally went to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the xiá offering. Fu Bi, a chief councilor, was appointed Grandee of the Xiá Offering; Han Qi, Master of Ceremonies; Song Qi, Commissioner of the Privy Council, Master of Insignia; Zeng Gongliang, Vice Grand Councilor, Master of Bridge Roads and Relay Stations; and Cheng Kan, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, Master of the Imperial Guard.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiayou, Emperor Renzong personally went to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the xiá offering. Fu Bi, a chief councilor, was appointed Grandee of the Xiá Offering; Han Qi, Master of Ceremonies; Song Xiang, Commissioner of the Privy Council, Master of Insignia; Zeng Gongliang, Vice Grand Councilor, Master of Bridge Roads and Relay Stations; and Cheng Kan, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, Master of the Imperial Guard.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宋庠 is Song Xiang, not Song Qi.

proposals.before: When three empress dowagers were ranked together in a dì sacrifice during the Dazhun era, critics condemned the practice as improper.
proposals.after: When three empress dowagers were ranked together in a dì sacrifice during the Dashun era, critics condemned the practice as improper.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大順 is Dashun (Tang Zhaozong), not Dazhun.

proposals.before: Therefore in the Dazhun era, when three empress dowagers were ranked together in the dì sacrifice, deliberators criticized this as contrary to ritual.
proposals.after: Therefore in the Dashun era, when three empress dowagers were ranked together in the dì sacrifice, deliberators criticized this as contrary to ritual.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大順 is Dashun, not Dazhun.

proposals.before: Two schools of interpretation emerged: Master Zheng's 'three before, two after' holds that a xiá follows a dì by twelve months, and a dì follows a xiá by eighteen months.
proposals.after: Two schools of interpretation emerged: Master Zheng's 'three before, two after' holds that a xiá follows a dì by forty-two months, and a dì follows a xiá by eighteen months.
proposals.reason: Chinese 禘後四十二月而祫 means forty-two months after the dì comes the xiá, not twelve.

proposals.before: These further divide into two schools: Master Zheng says 'three before, two after,' meaning that twelve months after a dì comes a xiá, and eighteen months after a xiá comes a dì.
proposals.after: These further divide into two schools: Master Zheng says 'three before, two after,' meaning that forty-two months after a dì comes a xiá, and eighteen months after a xiá comes a dì.
proposals.reason: Chinese 四十二月 is forty-two months.

proposals.before: We ask that a dì now be performed eighteen months after a xiá, and a xiá twelve months after a dì, so that the rites are not performed too frequently and the spirits are not treated irreverently."
proposals.after: We ask that a dì now be performed eighteen months after a xiá, and a xiá forty-two months after a dì, so that the rites are not performed too frequently and the spirits are not treated irreverently."
proposals.reason: Chinese 禘四十二月而祫 means a xiá forty-two months after a dì.

proposals.before: We request that now a dì be performed after eighteen months, and a xiá twelve months after a dì, so that performing the rites is not burdensome and serving the spirits is not irreverent."
proposals.after: We request that now a dì be performed after eighteen months, and a xiá forty-two months after a dì, so that performing the rites is not burdensome and serving the spirits is not irreverent."
proposals.reason: Chinese 禘四十二月而祫 is forty-two months, not twelve.

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 樞密使宋庠; Song Xiang is correct, and Song Qi is a different person unsupported by this unit.
Literal likewise misrenders 宋庠 as Song Qi; Song Xiang matches the chapter text.
Chinese 大順 is the Dashun era; Dazhun is a wrong reading of 順.
Literal repeats Dazhun for 大順; Dashun is the accurate era name.
禘後四十二月而祫 means forty-two months after the dì, not twelve; the proposed interval is accurate.
Literal likewise misreads 四十二月 as twelve months; forty-two months matches the Chinese.
禘四十二月而祫 requires a xiá forty-two months after a dì; twelve months is a mistranslation.
Literal has the same twelve-for-forty-two error; the replacement follows 禘四十二月而祫.

claimRetractions.reason: Song Qi exists only as the bad English reading of 宋庠; accepting r0001 restores Song Xiang (already claimed in c0013) and leaves no source support for Song Qi.
